## Reply below. Tell us who you are, and what you would automate.

Copy the grey block below — there is a copy button at its top-right corner, or just select the text — then paste it into the reply box at the bottom of this page and fill it in.

Delete any line you would rather not answer. Only the fourth one really matters.

```
**Who I am:**

**Where in Texas I work:**

**What fills most of my week:**

**If I could hand one job to an agent tomorrow:**

**How long that takes me now, and how often:**

**Have I used an AI agent for work before:**
```

## What a useful answer looks like

> **Who I am:** Rick, CBI
>
> **Where in Texas I work:** Bexar and the counties around it
>
> **What fills most of my week:** Boundary and retracement, some ALTA
>
> **If I could hand one job to an agent tomorrow:** Pulling deed records and plats off the county site before I price a retracement. It is about two hours of clicking, and I do it three or four times a week. Half of what I open turns out to be the wrong tract.
>
> **How long that takes me now, and how often:** About 2 hours, 3 times a week
>
> **Have I used an AI agent for work before:** No, today is the first time

Aim at **desk work rather than field work** — anything you do at a computer that repeats, and that you could explain to a new employee in a few sentences. Say what makes it tedious. That part is the useful part.

There is no wrong answer here, and most of the room has never used an agent. "No, today is the first time" is the most common reply we expect.

## Before you press Comment

**This page is public.** Anyone on the internet can read your reply, today and years from now.

So: **no client names, no job numbers, no tract descriptions, nothing under a non-disclosure agreement.** Describe the *kind* of work. Never the work itself.

And assume the reply is permanent. You can edit it, but you cannot delete it — only a repository administrator can do that — and every edit keeps a public record of what it replaced. Write it as though it cannot be taken back, because it cannot.

Nothing else here breaks. Filling this in cannot damage anything, and nobody is grading it.

## What happens to your answer

These replies pick the next worked example. The pattern the session showed — **corridor → public data → flagged list → lead times** — works for a ranch boundary and an ALTA as well as it works for a highway. Which one gets built next depends on what is in this thread.
